description:
Group your shortcuts into a single taskbar icon, with a modern Fluent interface.

Taskbar Groups Fluent packs a set of apps into one taskbar button. Click it, or just rest the cursor on it, and a small flyout shows every app in the group, so the taskbar stays tidy and everything is one click away.
- A group can show a folder, read again each time it opens: any folder, or a Windows place like the Control Panel, This PC, the Recycle Bin or all your apps.
- A group that holds other groups pins them all to the taskbar, one after another, in its order and with its separators.
- Groups inside a group open beside the panel, like a submenu.
- Keep a group by the clock too, with its own icon in the notification area, and open groups instantly with a panel kept ready.
- Separators on the taskbar to space groups out, and inside a panel to split it into sections.
- Drag and drop files, folders and shortcuts onto the group editor or an open panel.
- Find installed desktop apps, Microsoft Store apps and browser web apps with accent-insensitive and executable-name search, and give any app an icon of its own.
- Use an image or a colour emoji as the group icon, with a built-in crop and zoom editor.
- Apps, folders and even other groups in the same group.
- Real Windows 11 glass, and four panel layouts: grid, horizontal, vertical or list.
- Import groups from Taskbar Groups or AppGroup, and export your own to a file.
- Follows the Windows theme, accent colour and language (English, Spanish or Russian).
It installs for the current user only, so it never asks for administrator rights. The only network request is an update check against GitHub Releases when the app opens; there is no account and no telemetry.
Built in WPF and .NET 10 with the Windows 11 look. Some code comes from taskbar-groups and its fork pike-beta, both MIT.
